topic.name: Row Operations on 3x3 Matrices as Products of Elementary Matrices

question.text: Suppose that the elementary row operation $R_2:=R_2-3R_3$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
question.explanation:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation $R_2:=R_2-3R_3$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

\begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2&:=R_2-3R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E \end{align*}

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

question.text: Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order: \[ R_2 := R_2 - R_1, \qquad R_1\leftrightarrow R_3 \] What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
question.explanation:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the two given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is $R_2 := R_2 - R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 & := R_2 - R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_1 \end{align*}

  • The second operation is $R_1\leftrightarrow R_3.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 &\leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_2 \end{align*}

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 & 0 \\ -1& 1 & 0 \\ 0& 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to $E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_2$ on the left and get $E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 0& 0 & 1 \\ 0& 1 & 0 \\ 1& 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 & 0 \\ -1& 1 & 0 \\ 0& 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

question.text: Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order: \[ R_2 \leftrightarrow R_3, \qquad R_1 := R_1 + \dfrac 1 7R_3 \] What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
question.explanation:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is $R_2 \leftrightarrow R_3.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 \leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_1 \end{align*}

  • The second operation is $R_1 := R_1 + \dfrac 17R_3.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 &:= R_1 + \dfrac 1 7R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & \dfrac 1 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_2 \end{align*}

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 & 0 \\ 0& 0 & 1 \\ 0& 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to $E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_2$ on the left and get $E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 & \dfrac 17 \\ 0& 1 & 0 \\ 0& 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 & 0 \\ 0& 0 & 1 \\ 0& 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]
